intro.text: The legendary Blades of the Heralds, more powerful than ordinary Shardblades.
The Blades of the Heralds, given to them by Honor. They aren't spren, so anyone can use one, and holding one grants Surgebinding without a Nahel bond.

description.text: Honorblades, the Blades of the Heralds, are legendary treasures, more powerful than ordinary Shardblades. While one is summoned it changes the colour of its holder's eyes.
Honorblades were given to the Heralds by Honor. They aren't made from a spren bond, so anyone can use one, and each grants the Surges of its Herald's order.

items.text: Seven of the Honorblades are kept by the Shin, who have guarded them for millennia.
The nine abandoned Honorblades ended up in Shinovar.
Szeth uses Jezrien's Honorblade to kill rulers across Roshar between 1167 and 1173, among them Gavilar Kholin, King Hanavanar of Jah Keved and two Prime Aqasixes of Azir.
During the Battle of Narak Szeth fights Kaladin with it, and at the end he gives up his bond and it ends up in Kaladin's hands.
Kaladin passes it to Dalinar, who hides it in Urithiru and then gives it to Kaladin's men for training and for working the Oathgates; they swap it among themselves to keep its holder secret.
Agents of the Diagram work out when Eth holds it, kill him with a Shardblade and steal it. In time it's given to Leshwi, who passes it to Moash so he can join the Fused in the skies.
Talenel returns carrying his Honorblade, which doesn't vanish when he drops it. On the way to the Shattered Plains it's swapped for an ordinary Shardblade.
The Heralds carried Blades, each unique and covered in glyphs and patterns. At Aharietiam, the Last Desolation, nine of them left their Blades behind.
Anyone can use an Honorblade, not just a Herald; like a Shardblade, it can be bonded, summoned and dismissed.
Honorblades are made of Honor's own Investiture, which he splintered off himself and crystallised into metal.
Unlike Radiant Shardblades, Honorblades can't change shape.
Holding an Honorblade grants the ability to Surgebind without a Nahel bond.
Using Surges through an Honorblade takes more Stormlight, up to dangerous levels. The Shin still train some of their people to use the Blades and their Surges.
